recipes.title: Jollof Rice with Chicken
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of orange-red Jollof rice served with a piece of fried chicken
recipes.prep_alt: A woman stirring a large pot of stew over an open fire

sections.heading: Steps
items: Season the chicken thighs with salt, a pinch of curry powder, thyme, half the garlic, and half the ginger. Set aside.
Blend the tomatoes, red bell pepper, scotch bonnet, and half the onion (roughly chopped) into a smooth puree.
Ask an adult to help heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken thighs on both sides, about 4 minutes per side, then remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the remaining onion (sliced) until soft, then stir in the tomato paste and fry 2 minutes.

Pour in the blended tomato-pepper puree. Fry over medium heat, stirring often, for 15–20 minutes until it thickens, darkens, and the oil visibly separates and rises to the top — this step is what gives real jollof its depth.
Stir in the remaining curry powder, thyme, bay leaf, bouillon cube, and stock. Return the chicken and simmer 15 minutes, until cooked through.
Lift the chicken onto a plate. Stir the rice into the sauce so every grain is coated; the liquid should just barely cover the rice.

Cover tightly (foil under the lid helps seal in steam) and cook over low heat 20–25 minutes without lifting the lid, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Letting the very bottom catch slightly gives the classic smoky flavor.
Nestle the chicken back on top to reheat, fluff the rice gently with a fork, and serve.

recipes.title: Egusi Soup
recipes.dish_alt: A close-up bowl of thick green Egusi soup with visible melon-seed texture
recipes.prep_alt: A hand feeding melon seeds into a manual grinder

sections.heading: Steps
items: Season the meat with a little chopped onion, salt, and the bouillon cube. Ask an adult to help boil it in water to cover until tender, 25–35 minutes. Reserve the cooking stock.
Mix the ground egusi with a splash of water or reserved stock to form a thick, scoopable paste.
Heat the palm oil in a pot over medium heat, add the remaining onion, and sauté until soft.
Stir in the blended tomato and scotch bonnet, and fry 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Drop spoonfuls of the egusi paste into the pot, or stir it in smooth if you prefer — let it fry gently in the oil for 5 minutes to toast without burning.
Gradually pour in the reserved meat stock, stirring to loosen the egusi into a thick soup. Add the cooked meat, crayfish, and dried fish if using.
Simmer uncovered 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the egusi is fully cooked and a layer of oil floats on top.
Stir in the chopped spinach and simmer 5 more minutes until just wilted. Adjust salt to taste and serve hot with rice or pounded yam.

recipes.title: Suya
recipes.dish_alt: Rows of raw beef skewers coated in reddish spice on a grill grate
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Coating Skewers in Yaji Spice
recipes.prep_alt: A hand pressing ground spice mix onto meat skewers at a market stall

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Beef sirloin or flank steak, thinly sliced
Onion and tomato wedges, to serve

sections.heading: Steps
items: Grind the roasted peanuts fairly fine — this is the base of the yaji spice.
Mix the ground peanuts with the cayenne, paprika, ginger, garlic powder, onion powder, cloves, bouillon powder, and salt until evenly combined.
Toss the sliced beef lightly with a little oil, then thread it onto skewers (soak wooden skewers in water first if using them).
Coat the skewers generously and evenly with the yaji spice mix, pressing it on with your fingers. Let rest at least 15–30 minutes.
Ask an adult to help heat a grill or grill pan to high heat.
Grill the skewers 2–4 minutes per side, basting lightly with oil, until charred at the edges and cooked to your liking.
Sprinkle a little extra yaji spice over the hot skewers right off the grill.
Serve with sliced cabbage, raw onion, and tomato wedges alongside.

recipes.title: Nigerian Groundnut (Peanut) Soup with Chicken
recipes.dish_alt: A white bowl of deep-orange peanut soup with chicken and a dumpling
recipes.prep_alt: Packaged cones of fresh ground peanut paste at a market

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Raw peanuts, toasted and ground (or peanut butter)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Season the chicken with a little onion, salt, and the bouillon cube. Ask an adult to help boil it in water to cover until just tender, about 20 minutes. Reserve the stock.
If starting from raw peanuts, toast them in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until fragrant, then grind to a rough paste.
Heat the palm oil in a pot, add the onion, and sauté until soft. Stir in the blended tomato, scotch bonnet, ginger, and garlic, and fry 8–10 minutes until thickened.
Stir in the ground peanut paste (or peanut butter), mixing well and loosening it with a splash of reserved stock.
Gradually whisk in the rest of the reserved stock, a little at a time, until smooth with no lumps.
Add the chicken pieces, cover partially, and simmer over low heat 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the soup thickens and a thin layer of oil rises to the surface.
Stir in the chopped spinach and cook 5 more minutes.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot over rice or with a side of fufu.

recipes.title: Waakye
recipes.dish_alt: Waakye served on a banana leaf with egg, spaghetti, and stew
recipes.prep_alt: A tray of dried black-eyed peas ready to be soaked

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Dried waakye leaves, or pinch baking soda

sections.heading: Steps
items: Rinse the soaked black-eyed peas and place them in a pot with the water and the dried waakye leaves (if using).

Bring to a boil, then simmer 40–45 minutes until the beans are tender. Remove and discard the leaves — the liquid should now look reddish-brown. (No leaves? Stir in a small pinch of baking soda instead.)
Rinse the rice and stir it into the pot with the beans. Check the water level, topping up if needed, then season with salt.
Cover and simmer over low heat 20–25 minutes, without stirring too much, until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Meanwhile, make the stew: fry the blended tomato and onion in oil over medium heat 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Season with salt.
Ask an adult to help fry the plantain slices in oil over medium heat, about 2–3 minutes per side, until golden and caramelized.
Serve the rice and beans with a spoonful of stew, the fried plantain, a boiled egg, and a sprinkle of gari on the side.

recipes.title: Red Red
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of black-eyed pea stew alongside caramelized fried plantain slices
recipes.prep_alt: Bottles of bright red palm oil for sale at a market

sections.heading: Steps
items: Cook the soaked black-eyed peas in fresh water with a pinch of salt until tender, about 35–40 minutes (or use drained canned/pre-cooked beans to skip this step). Reserve a little cooking liquid.
Ask an adult to help heat the red palm oil in a pot over medium heat until it turns fluid and fragrant — don't let it smoke.
Add the chopped onion and sauté until soft.
Stir in the blended tomato, scotch bonnet, ginger, and garlic. Fry 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened and the oil starts to separate.
Stir in the cooked beans along with a splash of their cooking liquid. Simmer 10 minutes, seasoning with the bouillon cube and salt.
Meanwhile, fry the plantain slices in oil 2–3 minutes per side until deeply golden and caramelized at the edges.
Serve the bean stew hot with the fried plantain alongside for scooping.

recipes.title: Nigerian Pepper Soup
recipes.dish_alt: A white bowl of spiced pepper soup with meat, served with bread
recipes.prep_alt: Bundles of dried grains of selim and calabash nutmeg spice at a market stall

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Goat meat or firm white fish, cubed
Scent leaf or fresh basil, chopped

sections.heading: Steps
items: Season the goat meat with the onion, ginger, garlic, and salt in a pot, then add the water.
Ask an adult to help bring it to a boil, skimming off any foam. Simmer 30–40 minutes until the goat is fork-tender (fish only needs about 10 minutes total, added later).
Stir in the scotch bonnet, pepper soup spice mix, and bouillon cube. Simmer 10 more minutes to let the spices infuse the broth.
Taste and adjust the salt and heat level to your liking.
Stir in the chopped scent leaf just before removing from the heat.
Ladle the hot broth and meat into bowls and serve as is, or with a side of steamed rice.

recipes.title: Chin Chin
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of small crunchy golden-brown fried dough sticks
recipes.prep_alt: Two people cutting rolled dough into small squares on a table

sections.heading: Steps
items: In a bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, nutmeg, and salt together.
Add the softened butter and rub it into the flour with your fingertips until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.
Gradually add the milk, mixing just until a firm, non-sticky dough comes together. Knead briefly on a floured surface until smooth.
Roll the dough out to about ¼-inch (5mm) thickness.
Cut into strips, then cut crosswise into small squares or diamonds, about ¾-inch (2cm) pieces.
Ask an adult to help heat the oil in a deep, heavy pot to 325–350°F (165–175°C).
Fry the chin chin in small batches (don't crowd the pot) over medium heat, stirring occasionally, 5–8 minutes until deep golden and crunchy all the way through.
Remove with a slotted spoon, drain on paper towels, and let cool completely — they get crunchier as they cool.
